questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A cobalt(III) coordination compound has the empirical formula $\text{CoCl}_3 \cdot 4\text{NH}_3$. When $1\text{ mol}$ of this compound is treated with excess aqueous $\text{AgNO}_3$, $1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{AgCl}$ precipitates immediately. According to Werner's coordination theory, the primary valency and secondary valency of cobalt in this complex are, respectively,
questions.explanationEn: Precipitation of $1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{AgCl}$ per mole of $\text{CoCl}_3 \cdot 4\text{NH}_3$ shows one ionizable chloride outside the coordination sphere, giving the formula $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_4\text{Cl}_2]\text{Cl}$. In Werner's theory, primary valency equals the oxidation state of the metal ($+3$, satisfied by three $\text{Cl}^-$ ions) and secondary valency equals the coordination number ($4 + 2 = 6$). Thus, the primary and secondary valencies are $3$ and $6$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: For a square planar $d^8$ complex such as $[\text{PtCl}_4]^{2-}$ lying in the $xy$-plane, the highest-energy (unoccupied) $d$-orbital is
questions.explanationEn: In a square planar complex in the $xy$-plane, the four ligands approach directly along the $\pm x$ and $\pm y$ axes. This maximizes electrostatic repulsion and $\sigma$-antibonding interaction with the $d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbital, placing $d_{x^2-y^2}$ highest in energy and leaving it vacant in low-spin $d^8$ complexes like $[\text{PtCl}_4]^{2-}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following complexes exhibits the LOWEST molar extinction coefficient ($\varepsilon$) for its visible absorption band?
questions.explanationEn: High-spin octahedral $[\text{Mn}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$ ($d^5$, $^6A_{1g}$) has NO spin-allowed $d\text{--}d$ transitions; every $d\text{--}d$ transition is both spin-forbidden ($\Delta S \neq 0$) and Laporte-forbidden ($g \to g$), giving extremely weak bands ($\varepsilon \approx 0.01\text{--}0.05\text{ M}^{-1}\text{cm}^{-1}$). By contrast, $[\text{MnO}_4]^-$ has a fully allowed LMCT band ($\varepsilon \sim 10^3$), $[\text{CoBr}_4]^{2-}$ is non-centrosymmetric ($\varepsilon \sim 500$), and $[\text{Ti}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$ is spin-allowed ($\varepsilon \sim 5$).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: According to Taube's classification and crystal field activation energy (CFAE) considerations, which of the following octahedral complexes is kinetically INERT toward ligand substitution in aqueous solution?
questions.explanationEn: In $[\text{V}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$, $\text{V}^{2+}$ is a $d^3$ ion ($t_{2g}^3 e_g^0$), which has a large positive crystal field activation energy (CFAE) for both dissociative and associative transition states and no electrons in antibonding $e_g$ orbitals, making it kinetically inert ($k_{\text{ex}} \approx 90\text{ s}^{-1}$). By contrast, $d^2$ $\text{V}^{3+}$, $d^9$ $\text{Cu}^{2+}$, and high-spin $d^5$ $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ are all labile.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Among the following lanthanide ions, which pair shows the HIGHEST stability in the $+2$ and $+4$ oxidation states, respectively, in aqueous solution?
questions.explanationEn: $\text{Eu}^{2+}$ attains the half-filled $[\text{Xe}]4f^7$ configuration (large exchange energy), making $+2$ unusually stable for europium. $\text{Ce}^{4+}$ attains the empty noble-gas $[\text{Xe}]4f^0$ configuration, making it the only tetravalent lanthanide ion stable in aqueous solution (whereas $\text{Tb}^{4+}$ and $\text{Pr}^{4+}$ oxidize water rapidly).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following complexes can exhibit geometrical (*cis*/*trans* or *fac*/*mer*) isomerism?
questions.explanationEn: (A) Square planar $[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2]$ has *cis* and *trans* isomers. (B) Octahedral $[\text{Co}(\text{en})_2\text{Cl}_2]^+$ has *cis* and *trans* isomers. (C) Tetrahedral $[\text{Zn}(\text{NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2]$ has all four vertices mutually equivalent ($109.5^\circ$), so no geometrical isomerism exists. (D) Octahedral $[\text{Cr}(\text{NH}_3)_3(\text{NO}_2)_3]$ has *fac* and *mer* isomers. Thus (A), (B), and (D) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following experimental observations support a dissociative ($D$ or $I_d$) mechanism for ligand substitution in an octahedral complex $[\text{ML}_5\text{X}]$?
optionsEn: A positive volume of activation ($\Delta V^\ddagger > 0$)
A positive entropy of activation ($\Delta S^\ddagger > 0$)
Rate of substitution is largely insensitive to the identity and concentration of the incoming nucleophile $\text{Y}$
Increasing steric bulk of the spectator ligands $\text{L}$ strongly decreases the rate of substitution
questions.explanationEn: (A) True: bond elongation/cleavage in the transition state increases molar volume ($\Delta V^\ddagger > 0$). (B) True: dissociation increases disorder ($\Delta S^\ddagger > 0$). (C) True: because the incoming ligand $\text{Y}$ does not enter the rate-determining transition state, the rate is insensitive to $\text{Y}$. (D) False: bulky spectator ligands accelerate dissociative substitution by relieving steric crowding upon forming the 5-coordinate intermediate. Hence (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: For the high-spin octahedral fluorido complex $\text{K}_3[\text{FeF}_6]$, evaluate the spin-only magnetic moment $\mu_{\text{so}}$ in Bohr magnetons (rounded to two decimal places): _______.
questions.explanationEn: In $[\text{FeF}_6]^{3-}$, iron is in the $+3$ oxidation state ($3d^5$). Because $\text{F}^-$ is a weak-field ligand, the complex is high-spin ($t_{2g}^3 e_g^2$) with $n = 5$ unpaired electrons. The spin-only magnetic moment is $\mu_{\text{so}} = \sqrt{n(n+2)} = \sqrt{5 \times 7} = \sqrt{35} = 5.9161 \approx 5.92\text{ BM}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: If $n_1$ is the number of unpaired electrons in $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]^{3-}$ and $n_2$ is the number of unpaired electrons in $[\text{CoF}_6]^{3-}$, the sum $n_1 + n_2$ is _______ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]^{3-}$ contains low-spin $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ($d^5$, $t_{2g}^5 e_g^0$), which has $n_1 = 1$ unpaired electron. $[\text{CoF}_6]^{3-}$ contains high-spin $\text{Co}^{3+}$ ($d^6$, $t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$), which has $n_2 = 4$ unpaired electrons. Therefore, $n_1 + n_2 = 1 + 4 = 5$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: For the $\text{Pr}^{3+}$ ion (atomic number of $\text{Pr} = 59$, ground configuration $[\text{Xe}]4f^2$), the total angular momentum quantum number $J$ of the ground state is _______ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: For $4f^2$, the two electrons occupy $m_l = +3$ and $m_l = +2$ with parallel spins, giving $L = 3 + 2 = 5$ ($H$ term) and $S = 1$ ($2S + 1 = 3$). Because the $4f$ subshell is less than half-filled, Hund's third rule gives $J = |L - S| = |5 - 1| = 4$ (ground state $^3H_4$).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: For the neutral octahedral tris-chelate complex $[\text{Co}(\text{gly})_3]$ (where $\text{gly}^- = \text{H}_2\text{NCH}_2\text{CO}_2^-$ is an unsymmetrical bidentate ligand), the total number of geometrical isomers and the total number of stereoisomers (including enantiomers) are, respectively,
questions.explanationEn: An octahedral $[\text{M}(\text{AB})_3]$ complex forms $2$ geometrical isomers: *fac* (all three N donors on one face, $C_3$ symmetry) and *mer* (three N donors on a meridian, $C_1$ symmetry). Neither $C_3$ nor $C_1$ possesses any improper symmetry element ($\sigma, i, S_n$), so BOTH *fac* and *mer* exist as $\Delta/\Lambda$ enantiomeric pairs. Hence there are $2$ geometrical isomers and $2 \times 2 = 4$ total stereoisomers.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In the Tanabe-Sugano diagram for an octahedral $d^6$ complex, a vertical discontinuity occurs at $\Delta_o / B \approx 20$. At this critical ligand field strength, the ground state changes from
questions.explanationEn: For octahedral $d^6$, the weak-field (high-spin) configuration is $t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$ with ground state $^5T_{2g}$. As $\Delta_o / B$ increases beyond $\sim 20$, the strong-field (low-spin) configuration $t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$ with ground state $^1A_{1g}$ drops below $^5T_{2g}$, causing a change in ground state (marked by the vertical line in the $d^6$ Tanabe-Sugano diagram).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: For an octahedral low-spin $d^5$ complex such as $\text{K}_3[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]$ ($^2T_{2g}$ ground state), as the temperature is lowered from $300\text{ K}$ toward $0\text{ K}$, the effective magnetic moment $\mu_{\text{eff}}$
optionsEn: drops sharply to $0\text{ BM}$ because $J = 0$ is the lowest spin-orbit level
remains strictly constant at $1.73\text{ BM}$ at all temperatures
decreases from $\sim 2.3\text{ BM}$ toward the spin-only value of $1.73\text{ BM}$
questions.explanationEn: In low-spin $d^5$ ($t_{2g}^5$, $^2T_{2g}$), spin-orbit coupling splits $^2T_{2g}$ into a lower-energy Kramers doublet ($J' = 1/2$, with $\mu = 1.73\text{ BM}$) and a higher-energy quartet ($J' = 3/2$). At $300\text{ K}$, thermal population of the $J' = 3/2$ level and orbital contribution raise $\mu_{\text{eff}}$ to $\sim 2.3\text{ BM}$; upon cooling toward $0\text{ K}$, only the $J' = 1/2$ ground doublet remains populated, so $\mu_{\text{eff}}$ decreases smoothly toward $1.73\text{ BM}$ (Kotani behavior).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: For an outer-sphere electron transfer cross-reaction between two redox couples with self-exchange rate constants $k_{11} = 4.0\text{ M}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}$ and $k_{22} = 1.0 \times 10^4\text{ M}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}$, and an equilibrium constant $K_{12} = 1.0 \times 10^6$, the Marcus cross-relation (assuming $f_{12} \approx 1$) predicts the cross-reaction rate constant $k_{12}$ to be
questions.explanationEn: According to the Marcus cross-relation, $k_{12} = (k_{11} k_{22} K_{12} f_{12})^{1/2}$. Setting $f_{12} \approx 1$ gives $k_{12} = \sqrt{(4.0)(1.0 \times 10^4)(1.0 \times 10^6)} = \sqrt{4.0 \times 10^{10}} = 2.0e+05\text{ M}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}$ (i.e., $2.0 \times 10^5\text{ M}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}$).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: At $300\text{ K}$, the experimental magnetic moments of $\text{Eu}^{3+}$ ($\approx 3.4\text{ BM}$) and $\text{Sm}^{3+}$ ($\approx 1.5\text{ BM}$) deviate markedly from the simple ground-state formula $\mu = g_J\sqrt{J(J+1)}$ (which predicts $0\text{ BM}$ for $\text{Eu}^{3+}$ and $0.85\text{ BM}$ for $\text{Sm}^{3+}$). The primary physical reason is
optionsEn: breakdown of the $4f$ shell due to $4f \to 5d$ electron promotion at $300\text{ K}$
small spin-orbit multiplet spacing ($\Delta E \sim k_B T$), causing significant thermal population of low-lying excited $J$-states and second-order Zeeman mixing
ferromagnetic coupling between neighboring $\text{Ln}^{3+}$ ions in dilute solution
strong quenching of orbital angular momentum by the crystal field
questions.explanationEn: For $\text{Eu}^{3+}$ ($4f^6$, ground state $^7F_0$, $J=0$) and $\text{Sm}^{3+}$ ($4f^5$, ground state $^6H_{5/2}$), the energy separation to the first excited spin-orbit levels ($^7F_1$ at $\sim 370\text{ cm}^{-1}$ for $\text{Eu}^{3+}$ and $^6H_{7/2}$ at $\sim 1000\text{ cm}^{-1}$ for $\text{Sm}^{3+}$) is comparable to $k_B T$ ($\approx 208\text{ cm}^{-1}$ at $300\text{ K}$). Thermal population of these excited $J$-states and Van Vleck second-order Zeeman mixing raise $\mu_{\text{eff}}$ well above the ground-state-only value.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following octahedral complexes are CHIRAL (optically active)?
optionsEn: *cis*-$[\text{Pt}(\text{en})(\text{NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2]^{2+}$ (with the two $\text{Cl}$ ligands *cis* to each other and the two $\text{NH}_3$ ligands *cis* to each other, one $\text{NH}_3$ trans to $\text{Cl}$)
questions.explanationEn: (A) $[\text{Co}(\text{EDTA})]^-$ has $C_2$ symmetry (no $\sigma, i, S_n$) and is resolvable into $\Delta/\Lambda$ enantiomers. (B) *cis*-$[\text{Cr}(\text{ox})_2(\text{H}_2\text{O})_2]^-$ has $C_2$ symmetry and is chiral. (C) *fac*-$[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_3(\text{NO}_2)_3]$ has $C_{3v}$ symmetry (three $\sigma_v$ planes) and is achiral. (D) When *cis*-$[\text{Pt}(\text{en})(\text{NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2]^{2+}$ has one $\text{NH}_3$ *trans* to $\text{Cl}$ (and one $\text{NH}_3$ *trans* to $\text{en}$, one $\text{Cl}$ *trans* to $\text{en}$), it has $C_1$ symmetry and is chiral. Hence (A), (B), and (D) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Identify the correct statement(s) regarding magnetic moments of first-row octahedral transition metal complexes:
optionsEn: For octahedral $d^3$ ($^4A_{2g}$), spin-orbit coupling reduces $\mu_{\text{eff}}$ slightly below $\mu_{\text{so}}$ because $\lambda > 0$
For octahedral $d^8$ ($^3A_{2g}$), spin-orbit coupling increases $\mu_{\text{eff}}$ slightly above $\mu_{\text{so}}$ because $\lambda < 0$

For tetrahedral $d^7$ $[\text{CoCl}_4]^{2-}$ ($^4A_2$), $\mu_{\text{eff}}$ ($\approx 4.4\text{--}4.7\text{ BM}$) exceeds $\mu_{\text{so}}$ ($3.87\text{ BM}$) due to second-order spin-orbit mixing with $^4T_2$ across the small $\Delta_t$
For high-spin octahedral $d^5$ ($^6A_{1g}$), $\mu_{\text{eff}}$ shows strong temperature dependence because of first-order orbital angular momentum
questions.explanationEn: (A) True: $d^3$ is less than half-filled ($\lambda > 0$), so $\mu_{\text{eff}} = \mu_{\text{so}}(1 - 4\lambda/\Delta_o) < \mu_{\text{so}}$. (B) True: $d^8$ is more than half-filled ($\lambda < 0$), so $\mu_{\text{eff}} > \mu_{\text{so}}$. (C) True: in $T_d$ $d^7$, $\lambda < 0$ and $\Delta_t$ is small, making the second-order $-4\lambda/\Delta_t$ enhancement substantial. (D) False: $^6A_{1g}$ has $L = 0$ and no excited sextet states, so $\mu_{\text{eff}} \approx 5.92\text{ BM}$ is essentially temperature-independent. Hence (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements regarding the chemistry of uranium and actinide compounds are CORRECT?
optionsEn: $\text{UF}_6$ is a volatile, octahedral molecular solid that sublimes at $56.5\,^\circ\text{C}$ and is used in uranium isotope enrichment

In $[\text{UO}_2(\text{NO}_3)_2(\text{H}_2\text{O})_2]$, the linear $\text{O}=\text{U}=\text{O}^{2+}$ unit is surrounded in the equatorial plane by six oxygen donor atoms (two bidentate $\text{NO}_3^-$ and two $\text{H}_2\text{O}$)
The short $\text{U}-\text{O}$ bond length ($\sim 1.76\text{ \AA}$) in $[\text{UO}_2]^{2+}$ reflects substantial $\sigma$- and $\pi$-bonding involving both $5f$ and $6d$ orbitals of uranium
Unlike lanthanides, actinides do NOT exhibit an 'actinide contraction' across the $5f$ series
questions.explanationEn: (A) True: $\text{UF}_6$ is a monomeric $O_h$ molecular solid with low intermolecular forces, subliming at $56.5\,^\circ\text{C}$ for gaseous diffusion/centrifuge enrichment. (B) True: uranyl nitrate dihydrate has $8$-coordinate hexagonal bipyramidal geometry ($2$ axial oxo + $6$ equatorial O donors). (C) True: formal bond order in $\text{O}\equiv\text{U}\equiv\text{O}^{2+}$ approaches $3$ due to $\text{O}(2p) \to \text{U}(5f, 6d)$ $\sigma$ and $\pi$ donation. (D) False: actinides DO show a pronounced actinide contraction due to poor shielding by $5f$ electrons. Hence (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: For an octahedral $\text{Fe(II)}$ ($d^6$) complex with $\Delta_o = 22000\text{ cm}^{-1}$ and mean pairing energy $P = 17600\text{ cm}^{-1}$, the low-spin state is more stable than the high-spin state by $x\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$. Using $1\text{ kJ mol}^{-1} = 83.6\text{ cm}^{-1}$, the value of $x$ (rounded off to one decimal place) is _______.
questions.explanationEn: For octahedral $d^6$, $\text{CFSE}_{\text{HS}} = -0.4\Delta_o$ and $\text{CFSE}_{\text{LS}} = -2.4\Delta_o + 2P$ (relative to the free ion). The extra stabilization of the low-spin state over the high-spin state is $\text{CFSE}_{\text{HS}} - \text{CFSE}_{\text{LS}} = 2\Delta_o - 2P = 2(22000 - 17600) = 8800\text{ cm}^{-1}$. Converting to $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$: $x = \frac{8800}{83.6} = 105.26 \approx 105.3\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: For an outer-sphere electron transfer reaction, the total reorganization energy is $\lambda = 120\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ and the standard reaction free energy is $\Delta G^\circ = -40\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$. According to Marcus theory, the free energy of activation $\Delta G^\ddagger$ (in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$, rounded off to two decimal places) is _______.
questions.explanationEn: According to the Marcus quadratic equation, $\Delta G^\ddagger = \frac{(\lambda + \Delta G^\circ)^2}{4\lambda}$. Substituting $\lambda = 120\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ and $\Delta G^\circ = -40\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$: $\Delta G^\ddagger = \frac{(120 - 40)^2}{4 \times 120} = \frac{80^2}{480} = \frac{6400}{480} = 13.3333 \approx 13.33\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.
